coverage_note: Public employees of the State and its political subdivisions under the Industrial Relations Act, Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-801 to 48-842, administered by the Commission of Industrial Relations. State employees' bargaining and impasse procedures are in the separate State Employees Collective Bargaining Act (81-1369 et seq.), which this row does not cite.

governing_statute.value: Industrial Relations Act, Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-801 to 48-842
governing_statute.quote: Public employees shall have the right to be represented by employee organizations to negotiate collectively with their public employers in the determination of their terms and conditions of employment and the administration of grievances arising thereunder.

impasse_procedure.value: Mediation or fact-finding at either party's request, then a petition to the CIR, which may set wages, hours and conditions comparable to prevalent rates for similar work. Public employers cannot be compelled to sign a contract.
impasse_procedure.quote: Upon the request of either party, the commission shall require the parties to an industrial dispute to submit to mediation or factfinding.

agency_fee_status.value: Prohibited. Nebraska's right-to-work statute bars denying employment for refusing to pay a fee to a labor organization, and Janus v. AFSCME (2018) bars agency fees from nonconsenting public employees. A nonmember who chooses union legal representation in a grievance must reimburse a pro rata share of the legal fees.
agency_fee_status.quote: no person shall be denied employment because of membership in or affiliation with, or resignation or expulsion from a labor organization or because of refusal to join, affiliate with, or pay a fee either directly or indirectly to a labor organization
